analysis.title: The AI dominoes are starting to fall
key_insights: Tech selloff is spreading: Nasdaq sharply lower, semiconductors down 12% from their highs, small-cap tech down about 5% on the day.
South Korea's memory selloff is spreading to the rest of tech. KOSPI is described as one of the main pillars of the global AI trade.

NDX is back in the middle of its multi-month range, where the trend line in place since April and the 100-day moving average converge. The note says there is little edge in trading the middle of a range, but today's price action should not be dismissed.
SOX is down 12% from its October 6 high, well below its 100-day moving average and above its 200-day. RSI is at its most oversold level since late July. The level to watch is 11,200.
Small-cap tech is down 5% on the day, deeply oversold, with the 200-day moving average approaching fast.
EWY is testing its 200-day moving average for the first time since the KOSPI bull market began, with poor momentum.

sector_views.rationale: SOX is 12% below its October 6 high and below its 100-day moving average, with RSI at its most oversold since late July.
Down 5% on the day, deeply oversold, and approaching the 200-day moving average.

risk_factors: The tech selloff could be the start of a broader tech unwind rather than an oversold shakeout.
Weakness in South Korean memory stocks is spreading to the wider tech complex.
A break below SOX 11,200 and a loss of the 200-day moving average on EWY and small-cap tech are the levels flagged.
